rec.name: Tiered Package Feature Comparison Table (Product Image)
rec.status: Design requested — in progress (final graphic not shown)

what.text: A feature-comparison matrix shown as a product image in the PDP gallery. Rows list every service included in the Sectionfy Community, and columns are the three packages S, M and L. Green checks and red crosses show what each tier includes. In the source table, S includes 5 core services (Slack community access, A/B test insights, community challenges, templates & checklists, hypothesis database). M adds 5 more (case study library, online course, Sectionfy bonus, SectionBuilder bonus, weekly live call). L adds a monthly 1:1 live call and an individual CRO roadmap. The ticket asks for a clean version of this table, with no column highlighted, to be used as a product image. Another image in the ticket serves as the style reference.

why.text: Putting the whole offer into one scannable grid makes the value of each tier clear at a glance. Visitors compare tiers without reading long copy. The crosses in the lower tiers create a natural upgrade pull toward M and L (decoy / good-better-best framing), which can raise average package value. Because the table is an image in the gallery, it appears in the first place a buyer looks.

how.text: 1) Take the service-vs-tier table as the content base (rows = services, columns = S/M/L). 2) Design it in Figma in the brand style of the reference image: dark background, light row bands, bold row labels, green checks and red crosses. 3) Do NOT highlight any column. The reference image highlights the Sectionfy column, but here that was explicitly excluded. 4) Export as a square product image and upload it to the product's media gallery, ideally as the 2nd–3rd image after the hero shot. 5) Keep the Figma link for later edits. The same table can also be rebuilt as native HTML for accessibility if needed.

items: Check/cross mark per row and tier
Whether any column is highlighted (here: none)
Image position in the product gallery
Headline and subline above the table (optional, as in the reference image)

dependencies.text: A design tool (Figma) and a designer to produce the graphic. The product (Community packages S/M/L) must exist in the Shopify backend with a media gallery. No metafields or apps are needed if the table is a static image. The surrounding landing page also needs a Problem–Agitation–Solution block, a hero banner, and a case study section, which are separate pieces of work.

items: Tier mix (share of S vs M vs L purchases)
PDP bounce rate and scroll depth

images.caption: Source content: service-vs-package matrix (S/M/L) with checks and crosses, to be turned into the new product image.
Style reference: dark comparison-table graphic with check/cross marks and a highlighted column (the highlight is NOT to be copied for the new image).
